clue.text: Tot had rum, getting drunk in college

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters before it lurch into a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A toddler swigs rum and ends up tipsy at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmouth is an Ivy League college in New Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmouth College is a famous American institution of higher learning, an example of the category named.

clue.text: First lady supporting drive to cut wax

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece holds up from below, so the first lady comes after the drive letter

parts.note: D is the drive setting on an automatic gearshift
the first woman in Genesis
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A president's wife backs a campaign to reduce floor polish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means sitting below, so the first lady comes under the drive letter. 'Wax' is the verb, as the moon waxes, not polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow or increase, which is what something does when it develops.

clue.text: Dancer, say, gets cross with someone making a new catalog?

indicators.note: gets here means acquires, so something is added into the word just named

parts.note: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer; 'say' marks an example
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer gets angry with an archivist who is redoing the library card file.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer looks like a performer but is one of Santa's team; the cross slips in just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reindex is to compile an index or catalog again, so a reindexer does exactly that job.

clue.text: "British politician pockets silver" (that is the subject of a Rossini opera)

definitions.text: the subject of a Rossini opera

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Member of Parliament
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A headline accuses a British politician of stealing silver, then claims it inspired a Rossini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini's La gazza ladra is The Thieving Magpie, whose plot turns on a bird stealing silver, which fits the surface's pocketed silver.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Rossini's opera The Thieving Magpie is the silver-stealing bird.

clue.text: Obscure Australian birds avoiding a storyteller

indicators.note: avoiding something means steering clear of it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: obscure means not clear
the article, read as the single letter that goes
flightless birds native to Australia

explanation.surface: Little-known Australian birds keep away from a teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoiding a storyteller' looks like one phrase, but only the 'a' is avoided, and it is taken from the first word, not the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Remus is the fictional narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's collections of Southern folk tales.

clue.text: University held hostage by space-age computer in drag

indicators.note: a hostage is held inside by captors, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: HAL 9000 is the computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey
U is a standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A campus is taken captive by a futuristic machine dressed up as a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside HAL. 'In drag' suggests cross-dressing, but 'in' only links and 'drag' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something is to pull it along with effort, the same as dragging it.

clue.text: Introduction to Mr. Smith's Mrs.

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the title
Adam Smith is the economist; Smith's points to his first name

explanation.surface: Presenting Mr. Smith's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations, supplies the given name.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is the formal title for a married woman, the word that Mrs. abbreviates historically as mistress.

clue.text: A diminutive house of worship in Moorish Spain? There's a lot of buzz about it!

definitions.text: A diminutive house of worship in Moorish Spain?
definitions.meaning: fanciful meaning: a little mosque, with the Spanish diminutive ending -ito

definitions.text: There's a lot of buzz about it!

explanation.walkthrough: Spanish makes things small with -ito, so a small mosque would be a mosquito; the question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito is the insect famous for its high whine around your ears, so buzz surrounds it.

clue.text: Bit of lacquer found in skillful pottery

indicators.note: something found in a thing is located inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: deft means skillful

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just one letter from the start of the word

parts.note: the opening letter of lacquer

explanation.surface: A trace of glaze shows up on finely made ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: Delft is a Dutch town whose tin-glazed earthenware took its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white glazed earthenware named for the Dutch town where it was made.

clue.text: Amazingly, reclaim wine from water

indicators.note: something done amazingly is done in a startling, transforming way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somehow, someone recovers wine out of plain water.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning water into wine at Cana is the first miracle of Jesus in John's Gospel, so the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical changing of water into wine at the Cana wedding is the classic instance of a supernatural wonder.

clue.text: Feeling jealous after losing a certain dash in competition

indicators.note: after losing something, what is left lacks it, so some letters drop away

parts.note: envying is feeling jealous of someone
an en dash is one particular kind of dash

explanation.surface: Someone grows envious after missing out in a short race.
explanation.walkthrough: EN comes off the front of ENVYING. The dash looks like a sprint, but it is the punctuation mark, the en dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Vying means striving against others, which is being in competition with them.

clue.text: Lawyer's matters: taking time out and sending back a cameo

indicators.note: taking something out removes it, and time is the abbreviation T

parts.note: to count is to matter

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so it reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: a cameo is a small acting part

explanation.surface: An attorney's affairs involve taking a break and returning a carved brooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawyer's' is 'Lawyer is', with the 's as link. A cameo here is not a brooch but a brief walk-on part in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a counselor, or counselor-at-law, is an attorney who advises and represents clients.

clue.text: Once-angry Brits smash tiles around engineered dud

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one set of letters wraps the other
something engineered is constructed afresh, so the letters next to it are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: smashing something breaks it into pieces that land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Formerly furious Britons break tiles around a faulty machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the Luddites' story itself: early nineteenth-century English textile workers who wrecked the machines they blamed for their lost jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were English workers of the 1810s who rioted against mechanised looms, so they were Britons angry long ago.

clue.text: Curtis Strange is a bumpkin

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the name's letters turn up in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that Curtis Strange, the American golfer, is a country yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: Curtis Strange is a two-time US Open golf champion; his surname is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is an unsophisticated country person, the same sort of yokel as a bumpkin.

clue.text: Pet heading up by train to West and North Hollywood

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading up means travelling upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a snit
the El is an elevated railway, as in Chicago
taken as written
W is the compass abbreviation
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone takes their pet by rail heading west and north to Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is not an animal: to be in a pet is to sulk, so it is a snit, which turns upward to TINS. 'By' joins it to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a slangy nickname for Hollywood, mocking its glittery but shallow glamour.

clue.text: Uncapped glue is associated with disease

indicators.note: removing a cap takes off the top, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: epoxy is a strong resin glue

explanation.surface: An open tube of adhesive is said to spread illness.
explanation.walkthrough: EPOXY loses its first letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Poxy means affected by pox, the name for several diseases such as smallpox, so it relates to illness.

clue.text: Flower from eastern harbor to lubricate what returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: E abbreviates east
a port is a harbor
oiling something lubricates it
eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: A bloom brought from an eastern port to grease whatever came back.
explanation.walkthrough: E, PORT, OIL and EH are joined in that order, then the whole run is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden plant with fragrant purple blooms, so it is a kind of flower.

clue.text: Typically, fashion underlies round area of a church

parts.note: O is round in shape
the nave is the main body of a church
the rage is the current fashion

explanation.surface: Usually, style lies beneath the circular part of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'underlies' puts the fashion word below the rest, so it comes last. The rage, as in 'all the rage', is the fashion of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means as a general rule or in the usual case, which is what typically means.

clue.text: Something nobody wants to get: armor to protect a sailing vessel?

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship
chain mail is armor

explanation.surface: A riddle about armor that would shield a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface reads 'armor to protect a vessel' as 'vessel's armor': junk mail is armor for a junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk mail is unsolicited advertising that arrives in the mailbox, which no recipient ever wants.

clue.text: Europe guts foreign language

indicators.note: foreign means alien or strange, so the letters before it are made unfamiliar by rearranging them

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Europe disembowels a language from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign language' looks like the definition, but 'foreign' is the anagram signal and 'language' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Portuguese is the Romance tongue spoken in Portugal and Brazil, an example of a language.

clue.text: Defensive wall section confines gorilla

indicators.note: to confine is to shut in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a part is a section
a gorilla is a great ape

explanation.surface: A segment of a fortress wall pens in a gorilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' looks like part of the definition, a section of wall, but it is the outer piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a rampart or roof, built to shield defenders.

clue.text: Distant mountaintop is property of MacDonald

parts.note: far means distant
the top of mountain is its first letter

explanation.surface: A faraway summit belongs to someone named MacDonald.
explanation.walkthrough: Old MacDonald had a farm, as the nursery song goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's song Old MacDonald Had a Farm makes his farm the property he is known for.

clue.text: Forgetting offensive formation, New York athletes play with soldier's gear

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so a letter drops from the team name

parts.note: the Mets are New York's National League baseball team
the T formation is an attacking setup in American football
a skit is a short comic play

explanation.surface: Ignoring the attacking plan, New York players fool around with army equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb but is the noun, a short sketch. The T formation is an American football alignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess kit is the set of cooking and eating utensils a soldier carries in the field.

clue.text: Sharpshooter ripens bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A marksman brings fruit to ripeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a hidden marksman who shoots accurately from long range, so a sharpshooter.

clue.text: Criticize instrument of the Confederacy?

parts.note: Reb, short for rebel, was a Confederate soldier
uke is short for ukulele

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek question about which musical instrument belonged to the Confederate South.
explanation.walkthrough: A Johnny Reb's instrument would be a reb uke; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to reprimand them sharply, the same as criticizing.

clue.text: Head of Sotheby's is taken in by boom and bust

indicators.note: being taken in means being held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a head is at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the auction house's name

explanation.surface: An auction-house boss is swept up in an economic cycle of boom and bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom and bust' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'and' is a link and 'bust' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust and bosom both name a woman's chest, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Friday with Ann in a region of Belgium

parts.note: F abbreviates Friday
Ann Landers was the pen name of a famous American advice columnist; 'with' points to the surname that goes with Ann

explanation.surface: Someone spends Friday with a friend named Ann in part of Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann Landers ran a syndicated agony-aunt column in US newspapers for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is the Dutch-speaking northern part of Belgium, so it is one of the country's regions.

clue.text: Elegant Arab chief, I hear

indicators.note: what I hear is what reaches the ear, so the word is spelled by its sound

parts.note: a sheik is an Arab leader

explanation.surface: A stylish Arab leader, so the speaker has been told.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, close kin to elegant.

clue.text: Nut confounding Haiti's cop

indicators.note: to confound is to mix up and confuse, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lunatic baffles a Haitian police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' sounds like a crazy person, but it is the edible kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is the green-kerneled seed of a Middle Eastern tree, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Start of putrid, stinking trick

indicators.note: the start of a word is where it begins, so its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of putrid
rank means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A rotten, smelly practical joke, like a stink bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a mischievous practical joke played on someone, a kind of trick.

clue.text: South Asian runs through almost a million

indicators.note: the answer runs through the following words, spanning their letters without a break across the word gaps

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, the middle word, and the start of the third read on in one run

explanation.surface: Someone from South Asia burns through nearly a million in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'runs through' sound like spending money; it is the signal that the answer sits inside the letters of almosT A MILlion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are an ethnic group of southern India and Sri Lanka, so a Tamil is a person from that region.

clue.text: Penny seizes rebuilt gun (or equivalent)

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: a penny is a one-cent coin in the US

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so the letters after it are rearranged

parts.note: letters taken as written, the bracket ignored

explanation.surface: A coin is stuck inside a rebuilt firearm, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides that 'or' belongs with 'gun' in the anagram; the rearranged letters sit inside CENT after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruent shapes are identical in size and form, so congruent means matching or equivalent.
